div.l: And certeinly / he hadde a mery note
Wel cowde he syngen / and pleyen on a rote
Of ȝeddynges / he bar vtterly the pris
His nekke whyt / as is the flour delys
Ther to he was strong as is a champioıı̄un
He knewe the taủerners wel in eủery toıı̄un
And eủery hostiller / and tapster
Bet than a lazar / or a begger
For vn to such a worthy man as he
Accorded nought / as by his faculte
To haue with suche sike lazares acqueyntaıı̄unce
It is nought honest / it may nought auaıı̄unce
For to delen with no such porayle
But al with riche / and sellers of vitayle
And ouer al there / as ꝓprofite shulde arise
Curteys he was / and lowely of seruise
Ther nas no man / nowher so v̉ertuous
He was the beste begger / in his hous
For though a wydewe / hadde nought a sho
So plesant was his In pⁱrincipio
Ȝit wolde he haue / a ferthyng or he wente
His purchas was wel better / than his rente
And rage he cowde / as it were a whelpe
In louedayes / there cowde he moche helpe
For there was he nought / lyk a cloystrer
In a thredbare cope lyk a poủere scoler
But he was lyk / a mayster or a pope
Of double worstede / was his semycope
That rounded was as a belle / out of the presse
Somwhat he lipsed / for his wantownesse
To make his englissh / swete vpon his tonge
And in harpyng whan he hadde ysonge
His eyen twynklede / in his hede a right
As don the sterres / in the frosty nyght
This worthy lymitoᵘur / was cleped huberd
A Marchaunt with a forked berd
In motle / and high on hors he sat
Vpon his heued / a flaundrissh beuere hat
His botes clapsed faire and fetisly .
